item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Voices Along the Way
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Voices Along the Way
item.itunes:author: Janice Osborn and Rob Marus
item.description:
Part of the Reckoning and Renewing journey, FBC members Rob Marus and Janice Osborn offer the sermon. Their theme is "What I Inherited," a return to the question the series began with. What did your family hand you, spoken or unspoken, about race, difference, or who belongs? They share what they've set down, what they've kept on purpose, and what they hope to pass along.
Readings: Psalm 121; 2 Corinthians 5:16-20; Matthew 5:1-16.
Sunday, October 18, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Which Jesus?
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Which Jesus?
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
First Baptist continues our five-week series, Reckoning and Renewing, a chance to look honestly at our own story and our nation's, the dark pieces along with the redeeming ones. Pastor Julie preaches "Which Jesus?" from Matthew 16:13-20, where Jesus asks his disciples, "Who do you say that I am?"
For two thousand years, Christians have answered that question in ways that have shaped the world—sometimes toward peace and justice, sometimes toward conquest and slavery—with Scripture quoted in defense. What do we do with the truth that white supremacy in this nation was sustained, in large part, by the misuse of the Bible, in the name of the Savior to whom we belong?
Readings: Genesis 9:20-27; Romans 12:1-3; Matthew 16:13-20.
Sunday, October 11, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Midnight in America
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Midnight in America
item.itunes:author: Rev. Kevin Peterman
item.description:
First Baptist's five-week series, Reckoning and Renewing, is a chance to look honestly at our own story and our nation's, the dark pieces along with the redeeming ones. When we can name what's true about the past without flinching, that past loses its power to hold us in regret or shame. The series moves us a step further into freedom: naming what we've inherited, wrestling with how scripture itself has been used and misused, listening to our own members' stories, and finally asking what faithfulness looks like as we walk forward together.
Rev. Kevin Peterman preaches "Midnight in America," from Acts 16:16-40, the story of Paul and Silas in jail.
Readings: Isaiah 58:6-9a; Acts 16:16-40; Matthew 23:1-7, 23-28.
Sunday, October 4, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.
